v.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so edge 2 is dead and upgrading it has little effect.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 does not reach the output, so upgrading edge 2 is nearly irrelevant.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is disconnected from the input, so upgrading edge 4 yields little.
Replacing a missing direct edge with a conv gains more than replacing an existing useful op.
Going from a cut edge to a 3x3 conv is a larger quality jump than replacing an existing op (floor effect).
Restoring a removed edge with a strong conv yields a bigger gain than upgrading an existing weaker op.
Removing a strong conv on a main output edge costs more than removing a weak op.
Deleting a 3x3 conv loses more accuracy than deleting a weak op on the same edge.
Adding a skip where the direct edge was missing restores the gradient shortcut, a larger gain than replacing an existing op with skip.
Downgrading a strong 3x3 conv to pooling loses far more than replacing an already weak op.
